topic: Journey into Chaos: Holomorphic Dynamics and Iterated Functions
target_audience: Undergraduate STEM students or advanced high school students with a background in basic algebra and complex numbers.

sections.title: The Feedback Loop: What is Iteration?
lecture_lines: Iteration means feeding a function's output back as input.
Imagine a number cycling through the same rule repeatedly.
This feedback loop creates a sequence of evolving values.
animations: Display the word 'Iteration' in #FFFFFF, then replace it with a looping arrow icon.
Show a box [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/box.svg] labeled 'Rule: $z^2 + c$' in #00FF00, with an input arrow and output arrow looping back.
Show a sequence of numbers (e.g., 2, 4, 16...) appearing one by one in #87CEEB.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Complex Plane as a Playground
lecture_lines: We treat complex numbers as points on a plane.
Squaring a point stretches and rotates its position.
This geometry drives the motion of our dynamical system.
animations: Draw a white coordinate grid (#FFFFFF), label the origin, and incorporate the playground icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/playground.svg] in the upper-right corner to signify the complex plane.
Label the x-axis 'Real' (#FFD700) and y-axis 'Imaginary' (#FFD700).
Plot a single bright dot at (1, 1) and label it $z_0 = 1 + i$ in #FF69B4.

sections.title: Orbits: The Path of a Point
lecture_lines: An orbit is the sequence of points generated.
Some points spiral inward toward a stable attractor.
Others escape, shooting off to infinity very quickly.
Some may wander forever in a repeating cycle.
Every point follows a unique path through the plane.
animations: Show the formula $z_{n+1} = z_n^2 + c$ in #FFFFFF at the top.
Place a point P1 at (0.1, 0.1) in #00FF00 and a point P2 at (1.5, 1.5) in #FF4500.
Animate P1 moving in a small, bounded spiral near the origin.
Animate P2 shooting off-screen rapidly as its values grow.
Circle the bounded path of P1 with a soft glow in #00FF00.

sections.title: The Boundary of Chaos: Julia Sets
lecture_lines: The Julia set is the boundary of these behaviors.
It separates points that stay from points that escape.
On this edge, movement is unpredictable and chaotic.
Zooming in reveals infinite, self-similar fractal patterns.
This boundary contains the essence of holomorphic dynamics.
animations: Display $c = -0.4 + 0.6i$ in #FFFF00.
Start with a blank grid and begin filling it with a pixelated gradient.
Colors transition from dark blue (#00008B) to cyan (#00FFFF) based on escape speed.
Highlight the sharp, complex edge of the shape in #FFFFFF.
Zoom into one section of the boundary to show repeating patterns.

sections.title: The Map of All Maps: The Mandelbrot Set
lecture_lines: We iterate the function z squared plus c.
The Mandelbrot set maps every possible value of c.
Points inside represent parameters with connected Julia sets.
Each tiny bulb corresponds to a unique fractal world.
It is the ultimate dictionary of complex iteration.
animations: Set $z_0 = 0$ in #FFFFFF and show the formula $z_{n+1} = z_n^2 + c$ [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/dictionary.svg].
Sweep the complex plane, coloring points that don't escape in black (#000000).
Reveal the iconic Mandelbrot bulb and cardioid shape with a #FF00FF outline.
Small thumbnails of different Julia sets appear around the main set.
Scale the entire view to show the 'mini-mandelbrots' along the filaments.

sections.title: Conclusion: Beauty in Complexity
lecture_lines: Simple mathematical rules generate infinite, non-repeating beauty.
These dynamics model everything from weather to fluid flow.
One simple equation contains an entire universe of art.
animations: Transition from the Mandelbrot set to a montage of natural fractals (leaves [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/leaves.svg], clouds).
Pulse the entire screen with vibrant, shifting rainbow colors (#FF0000 to #0000FF).
Fade everything out to a final 'Thank You' in #FFFFFF.
